attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The remaining gap is a uniform reduction from the full multi-plaquette endpoint box to the single normal-coordinate source direction B_v with explicit E_rem, including BCH source nonlinearities and possible boundary holonomy dependence.
steps: Write the endpoint box with the original heat-kernel plaquette action and insert a scalar source s X_v only as a derivative at s=0, preserving the same theory.
Use geodesic coordinates U=e^A at the endpoint. The product of heat kernel and Haar density is Gaussian times sqrt(J(A)), up to image and Hadamard-coefficient errors.

Expand log sqrt(J(A)) as -sum_alpha alpha(A)^2/24 - sum_alpha alpha(A)^4/2880 + higher terms. The quadratic term changes the variance gate but cannot create the fourth connected cumulant at this order.

Tilt the Gaussian by exp(s <B_v,A>). Under the tilt, E_s[alpha(A)^4] contains the term t_a^4 s^4 alpha(B_v)^4. Applying -d_s^4 to the quartic Jacobian contribution gives -24/2880 times the root quartic, namely -t_a^4 sum_alpha alpha(B_v)^4/120.

The connected log removes Gaussian Wick-square pieces, and the previously established null incidence identity removes the straight f f contact. Therefore the first surviving local endpoint contribution is the negative Haar-curvature kappa_4 term, plus image, BCH, and tail remainders.
Multiplying by the Wilson color prefactor (g_a^4/4)(T_F/N)^2 and summing endpoint incidences yields a concrete sign/size condition against M_G.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The leading coefficient and sign are computed, but the actual three-hairpin endpoint incidence matrices B_v and the regulator-scale tail constants have not been evaluated. Without those constants the branch has a valid estimate template, not a certified promotion or falsifier.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Endpoint heat-kernel kappa_4 curvature estimate for post-H,K Wilson null form

assumptions: G=SU(N), t_a is small enough that endpoint plaquette holonomies are exponentially concentrated in one injectivity ball.
The endpoint source is centered and linear to leading order in geodesic coordinates; BCH nonlinearities are placed in the certified remainder E_rem.
The connected log Z_v is used, so Gaussian Wick-square contractions do not contribute to kappa_4,v.
The straight-segment C_A f f commutator contact has zero contraction with the null incidence vector before endpoint localization.
Endpoint tails from neighboring collar boxes obey a same-regulator bound E_tail with no new boundary counterterm.
definitions: source object: heat-kernel plaquette-sheet endpoint box B_v for SU(N) with plaquette time t_a, Haar measure, locked Wilson color normalization T_F, and a scalar null-channel source X_v(B_v).
target object: the post-H,K endpoint contribution R_end(u) to the corrected Schur-Feshbach null form for the already fixed three-hairpin Wilson block.
controlled interface: replace the seven-point source stencil for d_s^4 log Z_v(0) by a heat-kernel normal-coordinate expansion with explicit remainder and the same endpoint-box regulator.

same-theory condition: the source derivative is taken inside the original heat-kernel lattice Yang-Mills endpoint box, with no boundary counterterm, no altered Wilson normalization, and the same collar/hairpin observables.
B_v is the Lie-algebra source direction obtained by contracting the endpoint plaquette flux insertions with the Feshbach null vector and the signed collar incidence matrix.
M_G denotes the positive Gaussian Schur-Feshbach margin already left after H,K and the safe Wick-square part are removed.

equations.label: endpoint source partition function
equations.valid_when: Valid when the endpoint plaquette holonomies are localized inside the injectivity ball and all outside sheet variables are either fixed boundary data or integrated with the same heat-kernel measure.

equations.label: local heat-kernel density with Haar curvature
equations.valid_when: Applies after choosing geodesic coordinates for a small endpoint box and excluding image terms by the heat-kernel off-diagonal bound.

equations.label: signed endpoint kappa_4 leading term
equations.valid_when: Requires the connected source log and the null-incidence cancellations already used to remove Wick-square and straight f f contact terms.

equations.label: SU(N) root quartic
equations.valid_when: Valid when B is conjugated into the traceless Hermitian Cartan and tr_F fixes the fundamental normalization.

equations.label: endpoint contribution to R
equations.valid_when: Applies after diagonal normalization of the Wilson block and after summing only endpoint boxes left by the straight-segment cancellation.

equations.label: promotion inequality
equations.valid_when: Valid when the remainder and tail bounds are certified uniformly over the endpoint collar regulator.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is a same-regulator endpoint stencil or character-series computation whose certified kappa_4 interval is more negative than the curvature bound plus E_rem, or whose tails make M_G+R_end negative.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This gives the first signed analytic estimate of the connected boundary-OPE polarization R_end rather than another symbolic threshold. It identifies the endpoint curvature source, its color/geometric factor, and the valid margin test.
candidate_lemmas.statement: In the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet endpoint regulator, after the Wick-square Gram term and straight f f incidence term have been cancelled, the scalar null-channel endpoint cumulant has a signed local leading term: kappa_4,v(B_v)=-(t_a^4/120) sum_{alpha>0} alpha(B_v)^4 plus controlled image, BCH, and tail errors. Thus the remaining R_end term is nonpositive to leading order and is promoted exactly when its certified magnitude plus tails stays below the positive Schur-Feshbach margin M_G.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot or quarantine if the full endpoint box cannot be localized in one injectivity ball or if BCH terms create uncancelled O(t_a^4) contributions of unknown sign.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if the evaluated root-quartic bound plus E_rem and E_tail is strictly smaller than M_G, or if same-regulator source data certify M_G+R_end>0.
control_decision.reason: The cycle produced a signed analytic coefficient for the endpoint kappa_4 term, but promotion requires evaluating the real hairpin endpoint incidence vectors and bounding image, BCH, and tail errors.

dependency_updates.description: The regulator now supplies a signed local kappa_4 coefficient from the Haar/heat-kernel Jacobian, not only a finite-difference oracle.
The endpoint-local non-Gaussian piece has leading value -t_a^4 root_quartic/120 before the Wilson color prefactor and endpoint weights.
The derivation assumes the null incidence identity already cancels straight-segment commutator contacts, leaving only endpoint curvature and tails.
The stencil remains the numerical verifier for kappa_4 and can falsify the normal-coordinate estimate if certified intervals disagree.

falsifiers: falsifier: heat-kernel mass outside the injectivity ball is not exponentially small at the RG endpoint scale, so image terms can alter the sign of kappa_4.
falsifier: BCH nonlinearities in the endpoint Wilson source produce another O(t_a^4) connected term not included in the root-quartic curvature coefficient.
falsifier: a direct seven-point same-theory source evaluation of log Z_v gives a kappa_4 interval below the curvature estimate by more than E_rem.
falsifier: corner plaquettes break the null-incidence cancellation of the straight C_A f f contact, reintroducing a non-endpoint contribution to R.
falsifier: the certified inequality for M_G+R_end is negative after adding E_tail, yielding an actual finite Wilson OS determinant failure.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: The post-H,K R term is no longer a black-box endpoint cumulant: in the small heat-kernel endpoint box, its first connected non-Gaussian contribution is the negative root-quartic curvature of the compact group measure. This is a valid contribution-making move because it names the regulator, the cumulant d_s^4 log Z_v, the cancellations used, and the precise promotion/falsifier inequality. The branch is not looping; it now needs actual B_v incidence data and uniform remainder bounds.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the actual endpoint incidence directions B_v for the three-hairpin null vector, evaluate sum_v omega_v sum_{alpha>0} alpha(B_v)^4 using the SU(N) trace formula, and pair it with a heat-kernel C^6/C^8 remainder bound to certify the interval for M_G+R_end.

cycle_learning: This research cycle converted active route pressure into typed branch lemmas. The main mathematical change is that each branch now names a source object, target object, equation, validity condition, falsifier, and next experiment. Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
